description.p: Orcshot is a screenshot capture and annotation tool for Linux, ported from Windows Greenshot. Capture a region, a window, or the full screen, then annotate with shapes, text, arrows, and effects before saving, copying, or sending the result wherever it needs to go.

ul.li: Region, window, and full-screen capture on both X11 and Wayland
A full annotation editor: shapes, text, arrows, highlighting, blur and pixelize effects
Send captures straight to the clipboard, a file, or an external command

screenshot.caption: Annotate a capture with shapes, text, and effects

ul.li: Merges the three GNOME Shell extensions into one, orcshot@orcshot.org, published on extensions.gnome.org. The extension now calls into the app and exposes nothing on D-Bus itself, which is what the Snap Store requires. On first run, Flatpak installs it from extensions.gnome.org and Snap points the user there; nothing writes extension files into the home folder any more.
Replaces the Cinnamon panel applet with the app's own XApp status icon: no forced About/Remove menu items, nothing to install separately.
Flatpak: Save goes through the file-chooser portal, never writes into the sandbox's temporary folder, and never renames a portal-given file. Every file dialog is now a portal dialog.
Snap: the main window launches under confinement (it never did in 0.3.0), Save reaches the real home folder, and the launcher icon, desktop file and SVG images all work.
The "Saved as" dialog names the format that was actually written.
"Capture Window" is greyed out when no window can be captured.
An invalid placeholder in an external command's Arguments field shows an error message instead of crashing.
Adds Snap and Flatpak as real, install-tested distribution channels alongside the existing PPA.
Redesigns the tray to export a Gio.Menu directly on both GNOME and Cinnamon, replacing the AppIndicator3 extension API and the deprecated Gtk.StatusIcon.
Replaces GSound with bundled GStreamer audio for the capture-complete sound, which Flatpak previously did not play at all.
Fixes a crash when no X11/XWayland display is reachable during cursor capture, adds a "Reuse Editor" preference, and ships a redrawn logo.
